paper.title: On the Price of Privacy for Language Identification and Generation
paper.summary: Quantifies statistical identification and generation error with private finite IID samples.

formalization_scope.summary: All six main theorems in Sections 3–5 have Lean proofs, including pure and approximate privacy and the stated finite-sample constants in all three upper bounds.
specializations: The identifier releases a language and the generator releases a word. Both are randomized kernels on ordered IID samples with multiplicities.
gaps: Separate corollary, lemma and example inventories are outside this main-theorem count.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public finite-sample bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claim_inventory.scope_description: Six main numbered theorems of Sections 3–5.
exclusions: Rate corollaries, supporting lemmas, and appendix examples.
claim_inventory.notes: The PaperMap separately identifies Corollaries 3.5, 4.6, and 4.9.

lean_declaration_inventory.notes: The declaration index includes supporting modules.

claims.title: Private identification upper bounds
claims.statement_summary: The exponential-mechanism and Gaussian identifiers satisfy their privacy and finite-sample excess-risk bounds for an attained optimum.

source_assessment.notes: The earlier-index gap condition is expanded pointwise on a zero-based window.

formalization.notes: Both specified selectors satisfy replacement privacy and the displayed finite-sample excess-risk bounds.

lean_links.notes: The implementation proves privacy for the released index itself.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public finite-sample bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Private generation with a public witness bound
claims.statement_summary: Both mechanisms achieve generation with the stated public witness bound and mass-floor dependence.

source_assessment.notes: Public prefix counts have unit sensitivity and give margin n times the mass floor divided by two.

formalization.notes: The exponential and Gaussian generators meet both the privacy condition and the exact displayed error bound.

lean_links.notes: Any safe index in the window can be used as the comparison language, including the first one.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public finite-sample bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Private generation without a public witness bound
claims.statement_summary: A nondecreasing capped-depth penalty yields the generation error rates without a public witness bound.

source_assessment.notes: The mechanism maximizes the capped prefix score over every level. Its public inputs exclude the witness and mass floor.

formalization.notes: The exponential and Gaussian generators meet both the privacy condition and the exact displayed error bound.

lean_links.notes: Any safe index in the window can be used as the comparison language, including the first one.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public finite-sample bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claims.title: The cost of an unknown witness bound
claims.statement_summary: Pure privacy or exponentially small approximate-privacy slack prevents an exponential generation rate for finite classes with the stated overlap condition.

source_assessment.notes: A deterministic redirection of a small-mass infinite tail supplies the alternative distribution.

formalization.notes: The lower bound holds eventually for each positive exponent, for pure privacy and for sample-dependent exponentially small approximate-privacy slack.

lean_links.notes: All distributions supported exactly on the first language and both privacy regimes are covered.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public quantitative lower bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Two-distribution identification lower bound
claims.statement_summary: An intersecting private pair yields two attained-optimum distributions with worst-case excess risk at least (1−(1−exp(−ε))/4)^n divided by eight, including the nonprivate endpoint.

formalization.notes: Both inequalities, constants, and the infinite-budget endpoint are proved.

lean_links.notes: One pair of distributions works for every privacy budget, randomized algorithm, and positive sample size.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public quantitative lower bounds and their axiom dependencies.

claims.title: Two-distribution generation lower bound
claims.statement_summary: An intersecting infinite-difference pair yields two infinite-support distributions with worst-case generation error at least (1−(1−exp(−ε))/4)^n divided by three, including the nonprivate endpoint.

formalization.notes: Both inequalities, constants, and the infinite-budget endpoint are proved.

lean_links.notes: One pair of distributions works for every privacy budget, randomized algorithm, and positive sample size.

audit_refs.scope: Checks the public quantitative lower bounds and their axiom dependencies.
